reviews.review_title: The Gold Standard of VR Ports!
reviews.review_description: Roboquest was already proven to be a blast in its non-VR version, but experiencing it in VR takes intuition and immersion to a whole new level! What impresses me the most is how exceptionally well-optimized the standalone Quest version is—aside from the resolution difference, it feels almost identical to the PCVR version. The fact that it supports cross-platform multiplayer so you can jump into the action with players on other platforms makes it even better!

I never played the flat version before playing in VR. I didn’t think I’d like this game since I’m not a fan of some roguelike VR games. Well, Roboquest VR thoroughly impressed me. It has been one of the most addicting games I’ve played.  

Once I start, it’s hard to put down. The more you play, the more you discover. Each unlocked door or new discovery brings joy and excitement to keep going. 

After many hours of playing on SteamVR and Meta, I decided to give the flat version a try on PS5. I just can’t do it. It’s not the same. Being IN the game is so much more fun and immersive. For someone who rarely plays roguelikes, this is a must-have. 

If you experience any issues with the game, reach out to Flat2VR on their Discord server and they’ll fix it. Very responsive and reactive to provide a perfect gam

reviews.review_title: One of the best VR shooters out there!
reviews.review_description: If you've been thinking about getting this game, do it. It's great, it is just as good in standalone as it is on PCVR, this is a great version of the game that plays great. Plus, it has online co-op, which is so much fun with friends. There's is a lot to unlock and level up so always a reason to get back into it. Totally worth it! A must have for any Quest gamer out there.

Anyone who's a fan of intense, action-packed games is in for a treat


Robo Quest delivers this and does it with style.
You will die...and possibly a lot to begin with.
But there are multiple difficulties to help ease you in (and more difficult ones to unlock).

Being a rogue lite, with every success or failure you are getting stronger.

Whether it's via unlocking meta upgrades, learning enemy behaviours or how to specialise your perk choices

The sheer number of guns, perks, gadgets, classes and secrets will keep the game fresh.
You will be discovering something new every run for some time.

Despite spending 50+ hrs on PC, there are still many weapons/perks/builds that I'm still discovering.


The team has done a fantastic job at porting the game from flat and improved it, in so many ways (from being able to dual wield and fire at two separate enemies to adding in motion controls, e.g., for throwing weapons).
To something as simple as adding voice chat in co-op (which doesnt exist on the original flat version for some reason)

Thats right, there's Co-Op, and it's also cross-platform, so you can play with friends that have it on PC or PSVR2.

While there are some minor performance hitches (at launch), it is completely playable, and you probably would only be bothered if you played the PC/PSVR2 ports (standalone convenience!).

There's honestly some black magic going on in the background for it to even be able to run om standalon.
I'm sure the team will continue to polish it long after release if it follows the pattern to any of the other Flat2VR releases..

It was easily my VR GOTY when it came out on PC last year, and it's set to become Q3 VR GOTY.

What a great VR port!
It's a cel-shaded style robot shooter with roguelike elements, a rewarding progression, tons of missions, collectibles and secrets to find!
You like weapons variety? I think the arsenal is one of the biggest in VR games, with all kind of weapons... including weird ones: I laughed a lot seeing the reference to Trombone Champ!
How they could make it run so well on standalones is beyond me... visually is beautiful, all is polished and smooth (just the classic micro lag when loading), and it has a verticality I never expected: when you'll unlock the grappling hook or the jetpack, you'll discover the "upper floors" -which is mandatory if you want to find all collectibles-!
...and there's multiplayer, too!
Absolutely recommended!

Let’s start with the positives.

The gameplay loop is addictive. The gun play is really solid. The speed is excellent. ￼Overall it’s a really fun game to play.

The only real negative I have is the graphics. It is a pretty ugly game as it stands. The environments, especially are very stale and raw looking, and often flicker. Everything just kind of lacks the extra polish you would expect from a Flat2VR game. 

I’ve heard the devs mention improving the cell shaded art, and if this happens, this will become a five star review. However as it stands, it’s an ugly fun game.

Full disclosure: I received a copy of this game, but wanted to note that I would have easily paid $50 for this game. In fact, I gifted a copy to my nephew today so that I can enjoy playing it with him halfway across the U.S.. 

This is a MUST OWN VR GAME. 

As someone who has extensively played both the Meta Quest 3 and PCVR versions, I can emphatically state that it is remarkable what Flat2VR Studios managed to pull off in converting this fast-paced, roguelite, first-person shooter, and make it have the same fast action on standalone headsets with cross-play multiplayer support. I bow to their programming wizardry. 

RoboQuest VR is an instant classic, a fast and fun shooter that has so much to unlock & upgrade that I have easily sunk more than 60 hours into it and still enjoy going back for one more run. The runs themselves can be completed in under an hour (once you are good enough and know the various routes that will take you there in the shortest amount of time). Keep in mind that this game rewards exploration and is just as much fun to play as a solo game as it is a multiplayer experience.

The story is a human finds a half buried robot in the middle of a wasteland, fixes it up, and the robot springs to life, and leads the human towards the city, which has now been overtaken by hostile robots that wish to eliminate humanity. The games’ cartoonish art style and cut scenes make this a lighthearted and silly affair, but the action and coordination involved require skill at higher difficulties. In order to survive a full run (as the difficulty ramps up from location to location) players will need to learn about their enemies strengths and weaknesses, as well as each weapons strengths and weaknesses, and become proficient in using them (as well as their character classes abilities). Does this sound daunting and heavy? I assure you it is not, the controls are intuitive and there is an excellent tutorial that walks you through how to make the most of your abilities, but also encourages you to explore and figure some things out for yourself. 

And when I say weapons… I mean a “ratchet and clank-style”, massive armory; there are dual-wield weapons, melee weapons, manual reload weapons, energy weapons, larger, two-handed heavy weapons, deployment weapons which can summon support units (including bees!), and lots more to explore, including augmentations and alternate fire options. Customizing and upgrading weapons is a super simple process, players are also rewarded with the ability to practice with weapons back at base camp once they have reached enough proficiency out in the field with said weapon. 

Now to be clear, the graphics are excellent, and are about as good as you can get without sacrificing frame rate and speed, which is essential for making this game work. The cell shaded art style allows vast areas to be loaded onto a standalone headset, as somebody who has also played the PCVR version, I know that the detail is even better there, but that is the nature of standalone hardware and is not a fault of the game whatsoever. 

The bottom line is this game is essential for anybody hoping to get the most out of their VR headset. Purchase this game, support this developer, gift copies of it to your friends and play it with them, you will not be disappointed. Hope to be gaming with you soon! 

Note: I have seen a few reviews that complain that this game cannot run on Quest 2 hardware, that system is too old and does not have the chipset necessary to maintain a steady frame rate. Disappointed gamers must start to set expectations that newer games will only run on current hardware. IMO, an indie company like this does not have the resources to dedicate making a Q2 version (if such as thing is even possible). The game should not be penalized for such things.

If you like roguelikes and VR, this is an easy recommendation. Every run feels different thanks to the insane diversity of guns, which is also exactly what keeps me coming back for "just one more run" which somehow turns into five xD.
The controls and things to watch out for have just as much variety as the weapons so they can be a little overwhelming at first, but once everything clicks, it definitely won't disappoint.
My only complaint is that the game has somehow convinced me that getting destroyed by robots is a better way to spend the evening rather than with my family...

Roboquest is one of the most entertaining roguelites I have ever played on the Quest. The artstyle is colorful, and the different levels have a distinctive and unique look. It reminds me a bit of Borderlands. I love the story and the humor of the game 🙂 The difficulty level is adjustable for any Taste. for me it has a high replayability value - every run feels different and rewarding and I am sure that I will Continue to play Roboquest for quite a while.

Roboquest VR on Quest is an incredible tour de force, but also simply one of the best games available on the platform.
Roboquest VR is a roguelite shooter where you’re playing a robot going through levels partly randomly generated, smashing enemies robots in a cell-shaded environment.
The first time I played Roboquest, it was on a flat screen and I loved the incredibly fast pace; the variety of weapons, upgrades and Classes; the Rogue-lite mechanism; the basecamp as a haven between runs; the great cell-shaded graphics… and the music which supports incredibly well the fast pace of the game. But my first thought was how much better this game would be in VR. And this is where Flat2VR managed again something which I didn’t think would be possible: not only porting the game with full VR control, but also adapting the core game to VR: Roboquest VR totally feels like a game thought for VR from the grounds up. But maybe even more impressive is managing to port such an ambitious game on Quest. Yes, there are some concessions to the limited hardware, but it’s truly impressive how Roboquest VR feels and looks as an autonomous game. It’s the best of all worlds: everything which made Roboquest a fantastic game, but in full immersive VR; and squeezed into the Quest 3 platform!
While the gameplay is very welcoming to new players, the speed and verticality of the game means you probably need some VR legs to really enjoy it fully. But don’t worry: even if the game is easy to get into, it does offer plenty of challenges as you progress through the levels and the incredible variety of weapons and upgrades, which makes every run seem fresh.
Also, Roboquest VR comes out on Quest with a 2-players coop mode, with crossplay and voice chat. This is what the game needed to make it a full 10/10: being able to share the fun and run around smashing robots with a friend!
In conclusion, I don’t understand why you’re still reading this: just buy and play the game!!

This is one of the best VR games that I’ve ever played.  I've played over 200 hours on PSVR2, 125 hours in Steam PCVR, and after a few hours on the Quest, I'm pretty sure that this version is about to get even more play time than the other two combined.  At $29.99, this game is worth every penny!!  It’s an easy recommendation from me.

reviews.review_title: This is what VR is made for!
reviews.review_description:
This game feels like it was made for VR to start with. It is hard to believe it is just a Flat2VR remake because everything about it feels like it was meant to be. First person shooter, rougelike mechanics, tons of guns, upgrades, buffs with a comic book feel to it all. It is technically the same game, but now you are able to shoot in any direction you can get your hands and now you can do it with a friend or stranger.

The variety of guns and the simple shading does kind of give a bit of a Borderlands vibe to it. But, this is all robots with lots of bullets and mines and explosions everywhere. New weapons drop from time to time, but you are constantly picking up health orbs, wrenches, power cells and other collectibles. With upgrades at your base camp you can get characters in between levels to help you upgrade your current weapons, if you have a liking for them. Certainly helpful as you get deeper into the game.

Playing alone is pretty hectic at times, but with a friend, now you have twice the fire power and someone to come to your rescue, at a cost though. Robots survive with battery power and to charge one, you must take from the other.

If you like first person shooter games with roguelike mechanics, and want to play with a friend, this is certainly one to grab. 

This is my same review on Steam, but there are some slight differences with the Quest version as they had to reduce some quality for performance. However, it does not take away from the game at all. It’s just with the PC performance you do get crisper quality. There is cross-play, but each version of the game has its own save. So, your progress is not going to carry between the different versions.

Roboquest feels like it was meant to be played in Virtual Reality.  The movement, along with the variety of different weapons you get to use and foes that you go up against make combat great.  It includes the usual things desired in this sort of resetting, replayable, permadeath experience - new classes and items to unlock, new areas and enemies to reach, randomized weapons and upgrades. This game is just good plain fun.

This is a fast-paced roguelites shooting game. You have to upgrade to your preference with a new weapons that comes out ceaselessly during battle. Starting from pistol, there are melee gloves, bombshells shooter or sniper rifles, anything you can get. If you don't know what's good for you, you can keep changing this and that. You can also upgrade from base camp with the items collected during the game. If you die during battle, you have to do it all over again from start, but there is also a difficulty setting, and you can save it after completing each level and continue it again later. However, be careful because if you come out to base camp for an upgrade, you will lose your save point.   
I also beta tested it on PC, but it was so perfectly ported that I barely felt any difference in Quest alone. I feel the hard work of the developer team. Two-person cooperative play was also recently supported, and moreover, cross-play on PC and Quest is working well.
Since there is a fast movement, users who have not yet solved motion sickness should refrain. If you have solved it, I recommend it as the best shooting game you can play with your friend or family.

developer_response.body: Thank you, Carpedian, for the detailed review! We appreciate you pointing out the minimal difference between the PCVR version and the Quest version. It was our top priority to create the best experience within the Quest 3 and 3S' limitations, so that is a major compliment to us!

reviews.review_title: Excellent in 2D and in excellent in VR.
reviews.review_description:
I played the heck out of this game on steam. Movement is fast and fun like the good days of quake and Doom. 

Weapon variety keeps it interesting each run and the secrets and upgrades add tons of replayability. 

The VR version has a couple quirks I'm trying to get used to after spending so much time with the steam version. Nothing I can't get used to. 

Performance wise it's decent but I have had consistent frame drops and one crash in my hour or so play session. 

I'm still happy with it and am looking forward to playing this all the way through many times. I hope the devs add some more polish to improve performance on the Quest 3. Other than that this is an easy recommend. 

Thanks to the devs for making this port. We all owe you one.

reviews.review_description: Can i have some help installing it

developer_response.body: Hey Mr.Buzzins, you can try installing it via the game library in your headset, or open the Meta Horizon app on your phone, navigate to your game library on the app, and then install from there. If you have more than one headset, you might need to choose the headset you want it installed in. If you'd like dedicated assistance, please hop into our community Discord server and ask there. Someone will be happy to help you out step by step. Join here: https://discord.gg/bRbeKcXND9
